To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we verified 15 protein markers that can differentiate between Alzheimer’s disease and healthy controls, and 9 of these 15 biomarkers also differentiate AD from frontotemporal dementias.

a panel of cerebro-spinal fluid biomarkers was verified by a surface enhanced laser desorption/ionisation time-of-flight mass spectroscopy (SELDI-TOF-MS) technology which may potentially be used to improve the accuracy of diagnosis in Alzheimer’s disease (see also the abstract).
we verified 22 protein biomarkers that can be used to diagnose Alzheimer’s disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery and validation of novel protein biomarkers that can be used for early diagnosis of neurodegenerative diseases.
the development of a novel panel of biomarkers for differential diagnosis of AD and FTD.
the development of novel biomarkers for the early detection of neurodegenerative disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of the 7 markers (ABPP, ApoE, APOJ, C3, C3ar1, CD14, and C4) was able to discriminate AD patients from controls (AUC = 0.94) and from FTD (AUC =. 0.87).
the biomarkers in question are promising and may be of clinical use.

the combination of the 22 protein markers, which were verified in this study, is able to differentiate between controls and AD patients with an overall accuracy of 88.9%, sensitivity of 91.8%, and specificity of 85.2%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we verified the biomarkers that were previously found by the same group.
we have developed a novel panel of biomarkers that can distinguish AD from healthy controls and FTD, and that this panel is based on proteins that are secreted in the cerebrospinal fluids.
a panel of biomarkers for the differential diagnosis between AD and normal aging and between AD and FTD has been verified by SELDI-TOF-MS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of several biomarkers can improve the accuracy of diagnosis.
the panel of biomarkers is capable of distinguishing AD from controls with a high accuracy, and it is also capable of distinguishing AD patients from those with frontotemporal lobar degeneration.
we have verified a panel of biomarkers that are able to differentiate AD from controls and AD from FTD with a high accuracy.
